comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body: floating drawdown is what kills most challenges, since a lot of prop rules trail off the intraday equity peak and not the closed balance. does your warning trail from the peak including unrealized gains, or from closed trades only?

replies.author: F1RE_O_NEEK
replies.body:
That's the very reason I created it. Ordinary journals (such as TradeZella) merely record the closed balance, which is of no use when dealing with prop rules.

Because Ledgr uses an MT5 EA, it monitors your live, floating equity—taking into account both your unrealized gains and your intraday peaks—tick by tick. It automatically calculates your drawdown from the peak against which your firm has trailed and alerts you before you actually reach that drawdown.

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body: tracking the floating peak is the right way round, that's the number the firms breach you on. one thing to watch: if the EA samples equity at a different moment than the firm's own snapshot, your warning and their breach can disagree by a few dollars on a fast day.
